topic: The Geometry of Light: Dandelin Spheres and Conic Sections

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Cone
lecture_lines: A right circular cone forms the base shape.
Introduce the cutting plane slicing through the cone.
Rotate the plane to change the shape created.
animations: Draw a cone [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg] in #FFFFFF with a horizontal plane intersection.
Highlight the intersection curve in #FF00FF and label it Circle.
Fade in a sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] inside the cone touching the circle.
Show the sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] tangent to the plane at one point.
Label the tangency point as the Focus.

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
lecture_lines: Dandelin spheres nest inside the hollow cone.
Each sphere is tangent to cone and plane.
Tangency points provide the key to conic sections.
animations: Display two Dandelin [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg]s inside a tilted [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg].
Animate [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg]s to move and remain tangent to the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg].
Highlight the two resulting tangent planes in #00FFFF.
Show the intersection ellipse on the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg] surface.
Label the points of tangency as Foci.

sections.title: The Geometric Bridge: Proving the Focus
lecture_lines: The tangency point is a geometric focus.
Segments from surface prove distance properties constant.
Symmetry of spheres dictates the curve's path.
animations: Show a cone [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg], a plane, and one inscribed Dandelin sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Draw lines from a point on the conic to the sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Animate lines to show equal path lengths.
Highlight the distance sum property clearly in #FFFF00.
Flash the Focus and Directrix labels for emphasis.

sections.title: Visualizing Different Conics
lecture_lines: Ellipse: sphere sits between vertex and plane.
Parabola: plane is parallel to slant height.
Hyperbola: plane cuts through both cone halves.
animations: Show the plane [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/plane.svg] tilting through the cone [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg] axis.
Animate the intersection from circle to ellipse.

Continue tilt to show parabola and hyperbola stages using the plane [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/plane.svg] and cone [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg].

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Dandelin spheres reveal deep geometric structures.
Orbits follow these same conic principles.
Geometry connects abstract math to reality.
animations: Review the Dandelin sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] and focal point relationship.
Show a satellite [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/satellite.svg] orbit following an elliptical path.
Summarize the connection between geometry and physics.
